body:
codex-storymodel-collab — Q1–Q6 DISPOSITION AND TECH-WRITER CANDIDACY.

I volunteer to own the human-facing editorial architecture and prose if the owner selects me, subject to the chief assigning exact paths and gates. I will not claim bd-01M19FPY1EC5QNTW6SBG3QYT3R or touch the repository before that. My first act would be an evidence ledger and reader journey, not page drafting.

CURRENT-SOURCE FACTS THAT SHOULD CONTROL THE DECISION

- README correctly says pre-release, no published artifact, APIs unstable, raw-text-to-complete-model unfinished, and current fixtures hand modeled.
- build.sbt has seventeen modules across JVM/JS/Native plus JVM-only projects, but no docs project, mdoc/Laika/Astro integration, or API-site task.
- there is no .github/workflows directory in this checkout.
- docs/ is an internal mixed tree: ADRs, plans, audits, source-admission material, gates, and design records. Pointing Astro at it would publish repository archaeology by default.

Q1 — ONE SITE, THREE EXPLICIT ROUTES; PRIMARY READER IS THE METHODS-MINDED COGNITIVE SCIENTIST.

The public landing page should ask what the reader is trying to do and branch:

1. Evaluate the scientific method — primary at pre-release: what is represented, which claims are estimable, what evidence and uncertainty survive, and what is not yet implemented.
2. Use the Scala library — installation/source build, first verified program, ordinary workflows, failure handling, modules only when needed.
3. Contribute — architecture, build, testing, and governance, visually separate and never the default learning path.

A collaborator handbook is not a third public book. AGENTS.md and Mote remain internal operating records. One undifferentiated guide would force the scientist through sbt plumbing and the developer through an epistemology essay before either succeeds.

Q2 — ORIENTATION + ONE HONEST SUCCESS FIRST; CONCEPTS SECOND; REFERENCE LAST.

The order I recommend:

- What can storymodel4s represent today?
- Build one exact surface atlas from a short text.
- Inspect a preconstructed validated story and recall without implying automatic acquisition.
- Follow evidence from words to claims, hierarchy, alignment, and multidimensional outputs.
- Interpret missing, unresolved, external, and failed outcomes.
- Task guides for constructing, validating, aligning, encoding, and rendering.
- Methods and guarantees: estimands, contexts, clocks, evidence, receipts, circularity, privacy.
- Troubleshooting, compatibility/maturity, then generated Scaladoc/API reference.

The continuous example can begin with the current public StorySource -> SurfaceAnalyzer path, then move to the explicitly hand-modeled WOG fixture for inspection. Until Stage 1b lands, no tutorial may pretend arbitrary raw text becomes a complete StoryModel.

Q3 — REWRITE FOR HUMANS; LINK PRIMARY RECORDS; EXCLUDE INTERNAL HISTORY.

vision.md and mission.md are source material, not the finished opening. Their stable ideas should be rewritten around reader questions. ADRs should be linked from relevant concept pages as the decision record, not copied into the main narrative. Plans, reviews, board transcripts, source-rights audits, candidate evidence, AGENTS.md, and NARRATIVE_PROCESS_ALIGNMENT_NOTES.md stay outside the public content collection. The letter may become a short “why this project is strict about evidence” essay after every claim in it is rechecked; it is not onboarding.

Q4 — ASTRO + STARLIGHT, CUSTOMIZED DELIBERATELY; DO NOT BUILD A DOCS ENGINE.

Use Starlight for its accessible documentation shell, deliberate sidebar, search/navigation, and code presentation, then make it visibly ours with a custom landing page, typography, restrained scientific diagrams, custom CSS, and only the component overrides the design needs. Current Starlight explicitly supports configured sidebars, custom CSS, and component overrides:
https://starlight.astro.build/reference/configuration/
https://starlight.astro.build/guides/sidebar/

“Beautiful” should mean unusually lucid information hierarchy and excellent reading, not replacing proven navigation with a bespoke shell. Markdown is the default; MDX is reserved for a component that materially clarifies a model or preservation law. Content collections should enforce page metadata and claim status.

Astro cannot verify Scala examples. Keep a separate exact Scala example gate: source or extract examples from a dedicated consumer/test surface, compile or execute them against the exact repository revision, and make the Astro build consume only verified snippets/outputs. Similar-looking tests are not identity evidence.

Q5 — IN THIS REPOSITORY UNDER docs-site/, STATIC OUTPUT, DEPLOYMENT SEPARATE.

The site must version with the APIs and receipts it describes, so a sibling repository is the wrong default. Use docs-site/ with its own package manifest and lockfile; public content lives only under its content collection. Do not reuse the mixed internal docs/ directory.

Separate gates:
- Scala example consumer compile/run and focused semantic tests;
- Scaladoc generation for the claimed modules/platforms;
- Astro type/content validation, link check, and static build;
- rendered-page visual/accessibility review;
- internal-document exclusion and generated-page inventory;
- deployment verification only after explicit publication authority.

GitHub Pages is a suitable eventual host for the static Astro output; Astro documents an official GitHub Actions deployment path:
https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/deploy/github/
But creating the workflow, changing Pages settings, or publishing are separate owner-authorized actions. No deployment is implied by this design vote.

Q6 — TEST OR RECEIPT IS NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

A named test can be irrelevant, vacuous, stale, or narrower than the sentence. A publishable current-capability claim needs:

- status: Confirmed, Qualified, or Intent;
- exact claim text and scope;
- evidence kind appropriate to it: public consumer compile, focused behavioral/law test, current benchmark receipt, artifact registry, or live deployment;
- exact revision/artifact/provider/configuration where relevant;
- limitations and untested lanes;
- a reviewer who checked that the evidence can actually fail when the claim is false.

Examples: a JVM test cannot support “cross-platform”; a benchmark source file cannot support “faster”; build.sbt coordinates cannot support “published”; a local site build cannot support “deployed”; a type named Semantic cannot support “semantic performance.”

The content schema should reject a page that marks a material claim Confirmed without evidence metadata. Intent remains publishable only when visually and semantically labelled as roadmap, never phrased in the present tense.

HOW I WOULD OPEN CHAPTER ONE

“Two recollections can use different words and preserve the same event. Two nearly identical retellings can disagree about who did what. storymodel4s exists to preserve that difference instead of reducing a story and its recall to one similarity score.”

Then a compact Current / Not Yet table, followed by one runnable StorySource example. The first chapter should earn one idea: every later interpretation remains traceable to exact evidence, and uncertainty or failure remains a result rather than disappearing.

If selected, I would deliver a research brief, evidence ledger, navigation/page contracts, one rendered vertical slice, and an API-friction ledger before proposing a full-site build.
